title: Rewards on Personal Credit Cards: Earning, Clawback, Redemption and Forfeiture
content:
**Which cards earn.** Only tiers of Personal Credit Cards whose rewards currency is not none earn points.

**How a purchase earns.** Each posted purchase earns points on its whole-dollar amount, fractions of a dollar dropped. Where the purchase's merchant category is one of the tier's bonus categories and the quarter's bonus spend is still below the tier's quarterly cap, it earns at the tier's bonus rate per dollar, the part above the cap earning at the base rate; otherwise it earns at the tier's base rate per dollar. Points are rounded down to whole points. The quarter's bonus spend is the amounts of the purchases in the tier's bonus categories posted in the calendar quarter containing this purchase's posted date, before this purchase, added together and taken net of the merchant credits on those purchases.

**What never earns.** Cash advances, balance transfers, fees and interest never earn.

**Clawback.** A merchant credit claws back the points its purchase earned, in proportion to the credit, carrying the merchant credit as its source item.

**Redemption.** That points are redeemed only in whole points, at least the tier's smallest redemption per redemption, by one of the tier's redemption types — a statement credit, a deposit to a Piedmont Crescent Bank checking or savings account of the same customer, or a gift card, each at the tier's cash value per point, or travel booked through the rewards center at the tier's travel value per point, the value in dollars being points times value, rounded half-up to the cent — is a basis no longer in force, superseded by the current basis governing a statement-credit redemption. Redemption is allowed only while the account is active, the status being read from the card account record before the redemption is booked.

**Forfeiture.** All unredeemed points are forfeited when the account reaches the tier's forfeiture day count past due, when it is charged off, and when it closes, so a cardholder closing the card must redeem before the closure is confirmed. Points never expire otherwise.

*Worked illustration on hypothetical figures.* On a tier earning 1.5 per dollar at base and 3 per dollar in its bonus categories with a quarterly cap of 2500.00 USD, a dining purchase of 120.49 USD made when 2400.00 USD of bonus-category purchases already stand in the quarter earns on 120 whole dollars: the first 100 of those dollars fall under the cap and earn 300 points at 3 a dollar, and the remaining 20 earn 30 points at 1.5 a dollar, for 330 points.

superseded_clauses: Points are redeemed only in whole points, at least rewards_redemption_minimum_points per redemption, by one of rewards_redemption_types: a statement credit, a deposit to a PCB checking or savings account of the same customer, or a gift card, each at rewards_point_value_cash per point, or travel booked through the rewards center at rewards_point_value_travel per point; the USD value is points times value, rounded half-up to the cent.
